coveredBy: SY-06 (adjacent only: the sheet's close redraw and auto-open on return; it says nothing about state from another device)
UR-3.method: I searched findings.json for dayReview, dayreview.js and cross-device terms, and none covers it. I read js/core/dayreview.js:145-222 (due, recent, markShown, finish), js/modules/dayreview.js:30-51, 87-108 and 718-749 (openSheet, finish, maybeOpen, start), js/core/cloudmerge.js:400-460 (the leaf merge) and js/core/cloudsync.js:75-76, 150-168 and 1520-1554 (DEVICE_PATHS, BOOT_DELAY, the visible and focus pulls). On slot 40 at iPhone 402x874 I first ran KOS.cloudmerge.merge for four cases. Then I set up a due morning review (Sun 8 Nov, 09:00 slot) with ui.review empty and reloaded. I injected the other device's 'done' the way a merged pull writes it, and pressed the stale sheet's 'Skip review'.
UR-3.observed: The merge itself is fine. Device B, having only seen the review, takes A's done (state done plus doneAt). The leaf-conflict cases keep each device's own value: B's 'folded' against A's 'done', and B's 'skipped' against A's 'done'. In the app, the review auto-opened about 1.5 s after the reload (isOpen true, slot morning, seenAt written). The cloud cycle only starts after BOOT_DELAY of 3 s plus the network. When 'done' arrived, due() went to null and recent() reported done, but the open sheet stayed on screen (sheetStillOpen true; screenshot). Pressing its 'Skip review' rewrote the slot to state 'skipped' (skippedAt added beside A's doneAt). Because only B changed that leaf against the base, the next merge sends 'skipped' back to A.
UR-3.evidence: audit-evidence/2026-11/qa/verify-ur/ur3-merge.json; audit-evidence/2026-11/qa/verify-ur/ur3-sheet-open-after-remote-done.png. The code: js/modules/dayreview.js:747 is setTimeout(maybeOpen, 1500) at boot and :749 is setTimeout(maybeOpen, 600) on visibilitychange visible. js/core/cloudsync.js:76 is BOOT_DELAY = 3000, and :1548-1553 is the visible/focus cycle, throttled by MIN_PULL_GAP = 60 s (:75). js/modules/dayreview.js:101 is V().finish(st.slot, how), which only guards st.again. js/core/dayreview.js:216-222 is finish(), which overwrites state with no check of the stored state. Nothing calls reviewSheet.chip/maybeOpen or closes the sheet after a pull (grep for reviewSheet shows only main.js:186, hub.js, routines.js and calendar.js).
UR-3.rootCause: The state does carry across: state.dayReview.days is a synced keyed map and merges per leaf. The bug is ordering. (1) Auto-open decides from local state before the first pull of the open, at 1.5 s at boot and 600 ms after returning, against a pull at 3 s plus the network, or one skipped entirely within MIN_PULL_GAP. So the second device shows a review the first already finished. (2) Nothing reacts to a pull that closes the review: an open sheet stays open, and the chip only repaints every 30 s. (3) The sheet's finish writes blindly, so Skip on the stale sheet turns the other device's 'done' into 'skipped', and that propagates. The per-device ui.review.lastShown/minimised fields (state.ui) are correctly not synced.
UR-3.fix: (a) Hold auto-open until the first cloud cycle of this open has finished, or time out (say 4 s), when signed in. Have the cycle that ends call KOS.reviewSheet.maybeOpen. (b) After any pull, repaint the chip. If the open sheet's slot is now closed (done or skipped) on the merged state, close it with a short note ('Finished on another device') or turn it into the 'opened again' mode. (c) In dayReview.finish, never downgrade: a 'done' slot stays done, so 'skipped' is ignored when the stored state is 'done'. Optionally, add a merge rule that a closed state beats 'folded' and 'done' beats 'skipped'. (d) Add a smoke test with two docs that checks the sheet closes after the merge.
UR-3.harnessCaveat: There is no second real device or live Supabase pull in the harness. I simulated the other device's write by setting the merged leaf directly. The timing race (1.5 s against BOOT_DELAY plus network) comes from the code constants, and real iPhone or iPad network latency will vary.

coveredBy: EX-18 (adjacent: Exam Room keep-awake lost after switching away; not the Focus clock)
AX-03 (adjacent: Focus chime silent on iOS)
UR-5.method: No finding covers the Focus clock across a screen lock (I searched for visibilitychange, pagehide, distraction, idle watch and restore). I read js/modules/focus.js:83-110 (the wall-clock phaseElapsed and workSeconds), :392-445 (idleVerdict, noteActivity, the visibility listener), :446-528 (idleCheck, tick, heartbeat), :722-791 (bankForUnload on pagehide, beforeunload, the distraction listener) and :2526-2548 (restore). On slot 40 at iPhone size I faked Date.now and document.visibilityState to model a lock. A: hidden, 40 min frozen, visible, then tick. B: hidden, 40 min frozen, a tick BEFORE visible, then visible. C: a page kept alive in the background with ticks for 36 min. I then restarted the browser to exercise restore().
UR-5.observed: The clock does not stop while the page is only frozen. Elapsed time is wall-clock (now - phaseStartTs), so on wake the screen-off time counts as focus: A gave 45 min after 5 real minutes plus 40 asleep, still running. Three side effects showed up. (1) Every lock during a work phase is logged as a distraction: 1 after A, 2 after B, and from the second onward −2 HP when the penalty is on, with a 'Distraction #n logged' toast on return. (2) If the first tick after wake runs before visibilitychange (the order is not guaranteed on iOS), the idle watch fires its 'Still studying?' warning: idleWarnedAt was set, and a focus notification was pushed into the bell, though the visible event cleared it straight away. (3) If the page keeps running while hidden, the idle watch ends the session at 35 min (state idle, ended 'idle'). The case that matches 'the timer stopped' is restore after iOS discards the page: the session comes back PAUSED ('Focus session restored — 50 min kept, paused where you left it', restores 1; screenshot). It is credited only up to lastBeat, so the asleep time after the last heartbeat is lost.
UR-5.evidence: audit-evidence/2026-11/qa/verify-ur/ur5.js; audit-evidence/2026-11/qa/verify-ur/ur5-result.json; audit-evidence/2026-11/qa/verify-ur/ur5-restore.json; audit-evidence/2026-11/qa/verify-ur/ur5-restored-paused.png. The code: focus.js:2532-2538 credits time up to lastBeat, then sets S.state = 'paused' and increments restores. focus.js:775-781 pushes a distraction on hidden and drains HP past DISTRACT_FREE. focus.js:443-445 calls noteActivity(true) on visible. focus.js:488 runs idleCheck before anything else in tick. focus.js:747 is the pagehide banking, which does not fire on a plain iOS screen lock.
UR-5.rootCause: Invariant 4c makes 'recovery returns paused' intended for a reload or crash, and that is what a discarded iOS page goes through. Invariant 4d makes the idle end intended for an untouched page. But neither rule tells a deliberate screen lock apart from leaving the app: a phone's auto-lock is charged as a distraction, and a long lock that ends in iOS discarding the page loses the asleep time and returns paused. That reads to the user as the timer stopping. The frozen-page path itself is correct: the time is recomputed from wall clock on return.
UR-5.fix: (1) On visibilitychange hidden, bank the clock and write lastBeat = now synchronously (as bankForUnload does) so a discard after a lock loses nothing up to the lock. (2) In restore(), when the snapshot was running and the gap since lastBeat is under a cap (say ≤ 3 h, or bounded by the idle rule), offer 'Count the time the screen was off (N min)?' instead of silently dropping it, or credit it under the idle rule: up to IDLE_WARN past the last activity, then the 4d rule. (3) Do not count a hidden period as a distraction when it ends with no other page shown, or add a phone default 'Screen lock is not a distraction'. At minimum, let the user set the penalty from the running screen. (4) Run idleCheck only while the page is visible, or call noteActivity before the first tick after a visibility return, so wake order cannot warn spuriously. (5) Optionally keep the screen awake while Focus runs on a phone (KOS.desk's wake lock is already used for Focus; check it is re-acquired after visibility, see EX-18). Run a real-iPhone test before closing.
UR-5.harnessCaveat: Headless Chromium cannot lock a screen, freeze JS the way iOS does, discard a page under memory pressure, or show whether iOS standalone PWAs fire pagehide or pageshow on lock. I modelled those states by faking Date.now and visibility and by restarting the browser. Whether the user's 'stop' was a discard and restore, the idle end, or a missing wake lock needs a test on a real iPhone (stopwatch, lock 10 and 45 min, return).

UR-6.observed: Today a running Focus session is deliberately per device (invariant 33b): another device never sees it. A routine's step timer is not persisted even on its own device, so a reload loses it. Nothing offers handoff.
UR-6.evidence: js/core/cloudsync.js:160-168 (the focus.active comment and DEVICE_PATHS); CLAUDE.md invariant 33b; js/modules/routineplayer.js:37,53.
UR-6.rootCause: This is intended behaviour: the running timer is treated as a live process, not data, to prevent double pay (UR-4 and DI-04 show the danger of two live copies).
UR-6.fix: Design sketch, opt-in, per account. (1) Publish a small 'running beacon' instead of syncing focus.active: {sessionId, deviceId, mode, startedAt, phaseStartTs, phaseAccum, workAccum, state, subject/ref/assignmentId, untilTs, updatedAt} in a new synced key (for example focus.beacon) or an owner-only table, written on start, pause, resume, switch and end. (2) Another device shows 'Focus running on iPhone · 42:10 · Take over here / Leave it'. 'Take over' is an explicit handoff: it writes beacon.owner = thisDevice with a compare-and-set on the beacon's seq (the same CAS as __seq). The old owner, on its next pull or Realtime note, sees it lost ownership, stops its clock without logging, and shows 'Continued on iPad'. Only the owner may log or pay, and the session id stays the same, so KOS.sessions.log stays once-only (add a guard that refuses a second log for the same focus id, which would also close UR-4's resurrection path). (3) Routines: persist the player's {routine, day, step, stepStart} per device first (it currently dies on reload), then use the same beacon pattern. (4) Effort: medium. It needs a cloudmerge rule for the beacon (atomic, later seq wins), the Realtime channel to make handoff feel instant, smoke tests for two-device CAS and no double pay, and invariant 33b amended to 'the timer stays per device; its beacon syncs'.
UR-6.harnessCaveat: I did not exercise this with two real devices or live Realtime. It is a design note only.

UR-7.method: Searched findings.json for clip, Clip to page, inktab and Side by side: nothing covers it (SY-07, EX-38 and EX-04 are other ink issues). Read js/modules/inktab.js:50-100 (CLIPS and picture()) and 395-404 and 194-200 (clip, addPage). Reproduced on slot 41 at ipadl 1180x820: maths 2.1, Handwritten, Side by side; clicked a block, then 'Clip to page', for the memorise callout, the 'Where it appears' table and the kv table. Read the stored img items back from kurenai-os-ink and drew each one full screen for a screenshot.
UR-7.observed: Every clip with maths draws each formula twice: KaTeX's MathML layer as a second line under the visual layer ('a^m × a^n = a^{m+n}' then 'am × an = am+n'). Fractions and roots break apart (the 1/(2√2) in the table falls into loose pieces). Because the duplicated, unstacked content is taller than the original, the picture is cut off at the block's on-screen height: the callout stops at '(ab)^n = a^n b^n and', and the table keeps only half of its first row out of three. Separately, clipping when a new page has to be made repaints the whole tab, and the notes pane jumps back to the top (scrollTop 3069 to 0, the notes node replaced).
UR-7.evidence: audit-evidence/2026-11/qa/verify-ur/ur7-clip0.png (callout: duplicated laws, cut off), ur7-clip1.png (table: duplicated and broken fractions, only row 1), ur7-clip6.png (kv); scripts verify-ur/clip.js. Stored items are 860x348 and 860x570 PNGs. js/modules/inktab.js:61-67 PROPS (no position, top, left, clip, overflow, height, transform, vertical-align offsets); inktab.js:71-83 (computed styles inlined, classes removed); inktab.js:84-87 (SVG height fixed to the original rect h); inktab.js:199 (addPage outside view 'page' calls paint()).
UR-7.rootCause: picture() clones the block into an SVG foreignObject and inlines only the properties in PROPS, then removes every class. KaTeX hides its .katex-mathml layer with position:absolute, clip, height:1px and overflow:hidden, and it stacks fractions, sub/superscripts and roots with position:relative plus top offsets and fixed heights. None of those are copied, so the hidden MathML text appears and the vlists collapse. KaTeX's web fonts are not reachable inside an SVG used as an image, so the fallback metrics differ too. The foreignObject keeps the original height, so the taller result is clipped. A table inside a horizontal scroller is also clipped to its visible width. Clipping onto a new page repaints the tab through addPage, which calls paint() whenever the view is not 'page' (line 199). Minor: picture() has no guard for a 0x0 rect, so a detached block stores an item with src 'data:,' at 0x0. This happened in the harness with a stale node.
UR-7.fix: Rasterise differently. Either drop .katex-mathml (and any sr-only or aria-hidden nodes) from the clone and copy position, top, left, right, bottom, height, min/max sizes, vertical-align, overflow and clip, or better, render the block with a DOM-to-canvas path that embeds the KaTeX fonts as data: @font-face inside the SVG. Measure the clone's scrollWidth and scrollHeight (not the on-screen rect) for the SVG size, and unwrap a .k-n-tablescroll so the whole table is captured. Refuse w or h of 0. In addPage, when view is 'side', append the new sheet into the right pane instead of calling paint(), so the notes keep their scroll. Add a smoke that clips a maths callout and checks that the image height is at least the block's scrollHeight and that the clone holds no .katex-mathml.
UR-7.harnessCaveat: Headless Chromium can read the canvas back, so the stored clip is a PNG. iPad Safari taints the canvas and keeps the SVG data URL (inktab.js:88-97), but that SVG is built from the same clone, so the duplication and the cut-off should be the same or worse there. Not checked on a real iPad or with the Pencil.

coveredBy: SY-07 (different: background-redraw scroll reset, resolved on kos-redraw-1)
UR-8.method: Searched findings.json: SY-07 covers the panes jumping to the top on a redraw, and EX-38 the narrow docked bar. Neither covers scrolling into empty space. Read css/views/ink.css:117-125 and js/modules/inktab.js:443-482. Reproduced on slot 41 at ipadl 1180x820 and mac 1470x832: maths 2.1, Handwritten, Side by side. Measured #stage scrollHeight against the topic's height, listed the absolutely positioned descendants of the notes pane, and tested the effect of making the pane position:relative (the test style was removed afterwards).
UR-8.observed: The topic is 1023 px tall, but #stage scrolls to 1696 px (ipadl); on the Mac it is 1640 against 1015. Scrolling the page to its end scrolls the two-pane grid off the top. What is left is a strip of the notes pane ('Laws of indices — same base only') and then a screen of empty dark space, which matches the user's screenshot. 35 absolutely positioned nodes inside the notes pane (KaTeX .katex-mathml layers and SVG parts) have their offsetParent OUTSIDE the pane (.k-ink-side), and they reach y ≈ 7088. With .k-ink-side-notes{position:relative}, #stage scrollHeight drops to 1023, the topic's real height.
UR-8.evidence: audit-evidence/2026-11/qa/verify-ur/ur8-side-stage-bottom.png (grid scrolled away, empty page below a notes fragment), ur8-side-top.png; eval: {grid:[299,744], scrollers:[['DIV#stage',1696,760]]}; escaped 35 abs nodes, offsetParent DIV.k-ink-side; before 1696, afterRelative 1023. css/views/ink.css:118 (.k-ink-side sticky, fixed block-size), :119 (.k-ink-side-notes overflow-y:auto with no position), :124 (only clippable blocks get position:relative).
UR-8.rootCause: .k-ink-side-notes is a scroll container but is not positioned. Absolutely positioned descendants whose nearest positioned ancestor is outside it (KaTeX's hidden MathML in paragraphs, headings and lists, SVG parts) are not clipped by its overflow. They add their static positions to the scrollable overflow of the outer #stage, which then scrolls far past the topic. The sticky .k-ink-side cannot hold its place either, because its containing block (.k-topic-panel) is exactly its own height.
UR-8.fix: Add position: relative (or contain: paint) to .k-ink-side-notes and .k-ink-side-page in css/views/ink.css. Consider position: relative on .k-notes generally, because any overflow:auto pane holding KaTeX has the same leak. Add a responsive-audit or smoke check that #stage scrollHeight is no more than the topic's height plus padding with Side by side open.
UR-8.harnessCaveat: Measured in headless Chromium. On the iPad, WebKit's scrollable-overflow rules for escaped absolute children are the same in kind, and the user's screenshot matches. Momentum scrolling and scroll chaining between the inner pane and #stage were not reproduced with a real finger.

UR-9.method: Read js/core/ink.js:243-262 (inPoly, lassoPick), js/core/inkui.js:503-548 (addItems, selection chips, recolour, copySel, deleteSel) and 636-700, 771-773 (the lasso stroke). No finding covers it.
UR-9.observed: What exists: freehand or box lasso on ONE page surface. A pen or highlighter stroke is taken when 60% of its points are inside the loop. Any other item (image, text, shape) is taken when its bounding-box centre is inside. The chips are Move, Resize, Recolour, Copy and Delete. Copy duplicates in place on the same page, offset by 24 units; there is no clipboard. Each page is its own canvas and selection, so a lasso cannot cross a page boundary, and a selection cannot move to another page or another topic's notebook. An image is one atomic item: no crop and no partial selection.
UR-9.evidence: js/core/ink.js:251-262 (lassoPick: 60% rule for strokes, centre rule for everything else); js/core/inkui.js:510-547 (chips; copySel offsets +24 on the same page); inkui.js:504 (addItems selects on the same surface).
UR-9.rootCause: By design today: one surface per page (invariant 132), with selection state held by that surface.
UR-9.fix: Cross-page requests take three changes. (1) A desk-level selection: items lifted out of a page into a floating layer during Move, dropped on whichever surface the pointer ends over (the remove and add as one undo step on each page). (2) An in-app ink clipboard (dk.clip = items), with 'Paste here' on any page or notebook in the palette's More menu. (3) Image crop: a crop rectangle {cx, cy, cw, ch} on img items, drawn by drawItems and edited from a 'Crop' chip; the lasso cannot cut pixels, so 'parts of an image' means crop or duplicate-and-crop. 'Iffy': consider a stroke selected when its bounding box is mostly inside OR 40% of its points, show the selection preview live while drawing, and allow a tap on an item to select it alone. M-L effort, needs a design pass.
UR-9.harnessCaveat: How the lasso feels with the Pencil (accuracy, palm rejection) cannot be judged in headless Chromium. Only the code rules were read.

UR-16.method: No finding covers the head, aura or space; SC-29 covers only iPad portrait, where she is absent. Read css/views/assistant.css:22-33 (.k-asst-mascot motion vars: --asst-breath-lift 1.15%, --asst-breath-swell 1.012; .k-asst-mascot-frame overflow:hidden; the aura ::before inset 30% 12% 4%), :40 (hover scale 1.03), :58-63 (asstBreath translates up and scales from 50% 100%), :74-81 (working lift 1.5%, success -4.5%), :357 (.k-asst-presence background radial-gradient(70% 50% at 50% 38%)), :362-371 (stage, justify-content:flex-end, frame block-size var(--asst-fig-h)=440px, aspect-ratio 2/3 with max-inline-size 100%, object-position center, aura inset 18% 12% 14%) and :528-532 (presence hidden at ≤1080). Read js/modules/assistant.js:453-485 (mascotNode) and 2048-2063 (presence). On slot 42 I measured #/assistant at mac, ipadl and ipad. I read the art's alpha in a canvas and froze asstBreath at its peak in the 'working' state for a crop.
UR-16.observed: Mac: the presence is 300x772 and the stage starts at y=113, but the figure frame starts at y=256, leaving 143px of empty panel above her. iPad landscape: the stage starts at y=131 and the frame at y=244, leaving 113px empty. The frame is 275x440 (mac) or 215x440 (ipadl), not 2:3: max-inline-size clamps the width while block-size stays 440px. The art (605x1400) is contained at 190x440, so it fills the frame's full height with no gap at the top. The PNG has only 6 transparent rows at the top (~1.9 CSS px). The frame clips with overflow:hidden, while the idle breath lifts the image by 1.15% (5px) and swells it 1.012 from the bottom (5px). Hover adds scale 1.03 (+13px), 'working' lifts 1.5% and 'success' 4.5%. At each peak the top ~8–20px of her hair is cut by the frame edge (ur16-ipadl-peak.png: image top 237.5 against frame top 250.5). The panel's glow is an ellipse (70% x 50%) centred at 38% of the panel height (y≈353 on mac), while her centre is at y≈476. The glow sits ~120px above her and reads as an off-centre oval. The frame's own aura (::before, 18% 12% 14%) is a 209x299 vertical oval. At 820 (iPad portrait) there is no figure at all (SC-29).
UR-16.evidence: audit-evidence/2026-11/qa/verify-ur/ur16-mac.png, ur16-ipadl.png, ur16-ipadl-peak.png, ur16-ipadl-peak-head.png; numbers: mac stage y113 / frame y256 (143px empty); ipadl stage y131 / frame y244; img natural 605x1400, first opaque row 6; frozen peak img top 237.5 < frame top 250.5
UR-16.rootCause: Three causes. (1) The figure is drawn edge to edge in a clipping frame (object-fit contain, so the 0.43-ratio art fills the 440px height), and every 'float' animation (asstBreath lift and swell, hover scale, working and success lifts) moves her up past the clip. (2) .k-asst-stage .k-asst-mascot uses justify-content:flex-end (assistant.css:366) with a fixed 440px figure, so all spare panel height collects above her; the comment at :368 says 'she stands in the middle' but only the img's object-position was centred. (3) The panel glow radial-gradient(70% 50% at 50% 38%) (:357) is positioned in panel percentages, not on the figure. The frame aura is a percentage inset of a non-square frame, so it is an oval.
UR-16.fix: Give the frame headroom: pad the image box at the top (e.g. block-size calc(100% - lift) with padding-block-start equal to the max lift plus swell plus hover, ~4%), or set overflow:visible on the stage frame and clip at the presence instead. Centre the figure: justify-content:center on .k-asst-stage .k-asst-mascot (or let the frame take min(440px, 100%) and centre it). Move the glow onto the figure: draw it as the frame's ::before only, square (aspect-ratio 1 centred on her torso), and drop the panel's 38% radial or tie it to the figure's centre. Fix the frame to a true 2:3 (drop the explicit block-size when the width is clamped). Run node tools/visual_audit.mjs and the --ipad audit.
UR-16.harnessCaveat: The clip was shown by freezing the CSS animation at its peak. On a real iPad the breathing runs continuously and the cut flickers in and out, so a still screenshot may or may not catch it. Reduced-motion users (assistant.css:111-116) never see it. A live renderer (Live2D) is inert in this build.

UR-17.rootCause: Systemic: the coarse-pointer floor in base.css raises min-block-size to 44px on every button (zero specificity). Hand-rolled round controls set only inline-size/block-size or rely on a width set elsewhere, so the height grows and the width does not, against invariant 69 ('a round control must raise its width too'). AX-05 already names the shared-primitive root cause. The files chip is a .k-chip whose label 'All' is shorter than 44px.
UR-17.fix: One rule, not per-page patches. Add a round-control primitive (e.g. [data-shape=round] or a .k-round class) in components.css that, under (pointer: coarse), sets min-inline-size equal to min-block-size and aspect-ratio 1, and migrate the instances above to it: .k-ja-cp, .k-cr-day, .k-asst-day, .k-mind-kindpick, .k-dr-chip, and the code path squares (CO-01). Give .k-chip a min-inline-size of --hit-coarse on touch, which fixes files.subject 'All'. Add a smoke that, at a coarse-pointer viewport, fails any visible element with border-radius ≥45% of its short side whose w/h falls outside 0.95–1.05 unless it is marked as a pill.
UR-17.harnessCaveat: The sweep covers routes in their default state on the seeded account. Controls behind dialogs, menus, empty or first-run states, or focus rings (AG-06, AG-15, PR-08, AX-26) were not reached and come from the existing findings. Headless Chromium emulates pointer: coarse; a real iPad's Safari applies the same CSS, so the geometry carries over.

UR-23.method: Searched findings.json (no finding covers it). Read tools/cs-wasm/CsWasm.csproj (one PackageReference: Microsoft.CodeAnalysis.CSharp 5.0.0, with trimmer roots Microsoft.CodeAnalysis and .CSharp; no Workspaces or Features) and tools/cs-wasm/Program.cs:60-72 (parse into SyntaxTrees, CSharpCompilation.Create, comp.GetDiagnostics()). Checked js/labs/cs-wasm-worker.js (67 lines), js/core/codeui.js:5,104-112 (the editor is a textarea under a highlighting layer, plus a phone key bar) and js/labs/cs-interp.js:46 (lex) and :169 (parse); 3,395 lines in all. The built runtime assets/code/runtime/csw-1.1 is 29 MB.
UR-23.observed: Feasible in stages without new heavy packages. The full runtime (units 7+) already builds a CSharpCompilation and collects diagnostics on every run (Program.cs:69). A 'check' message that returns the diagnostics with line and column spans, without emitting, would give red underlines as you type, sent from a debounced (~600 ms) request to the already-warm worker. Completion of identifiers and types in scope works with the CSharp package alone (SemanticModel.LookupSymbols(position) plus the member lookup on the expression's type), so no Microsoft.CodeAnalysis.Features is needed. Rename across one program can be hand-rolled: GetSymbolInfo/GetDeclaredSymbol on every IdentifierName and compare with SymbolEqualityComparer. Roslyn's Renamer, CompletionService and SymbolFinder need Microsoft.CodeAnalysis.Workspaces and Features, which would add several MB to a 29 MB download and need trimming work. Units 1–6 (cs-interp.js) have a lexer and parser that already report errors with line numbers, so parse-error underlines and scope-based completion from the parser's declarations are possible there, with no type inference. The editor side is the bigger cost: the textarea-plus-overlay editor (codeui.js:104) has no caret-anchored popup or squiggle layer. Both must be drawn in the highlight overlay and be keyboard-accessible (invariants 66, 67) and touch-usable on the phone key bar.
UR-23.rootCause: Not a defect. The editor was built for highlighting and running, with no language services.
UR-23.fix: Backlog, in stages. (1) Diagnostics as you type on the full runtime: a 'check' op in Program.cs and cs-wasm-worker.js (compile without emit, return spans), squiggles in the codeui overlay, debounced, only once the runtime is downloaded (invariant 105: no fetch until asked). (2) Completion from LookupSymbols, filtered to the unit's stage language, in a listbox popup with ARIA combobox semantics. (3) Single-file rename through symbol comparison. (4) Units 1–6: parse errors and declared-name completion from cs-interp's parser. Keep it all inside the sealed worker, so the sandbox contract (no network after warm-up) is unchanged. Measure the warm-check latency on an iPad before committing.
UR-23.harnessCaveat: Feasibility only. I did not build or time a Roslyn 'check' round-trip in WebAssembly, and iPad Safari's WASM memory and warm-up limits were not measured.
